basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 35.' and it opens 'Vers. 35. Lugens in infernum. Hinc beatus Augustinus quaerit utrum soli mali ad infernum'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 35. Lugens in infernum. Hinc beatus Augustinus quaerit utrum soli mali ad infernum descendant, an mali simul et boni. Aut forte perturbati animi verba sunt. Sed credibile est fuisse apud infernum quaedam loca secretiora et minus poenalia ante passionem Domini, ad quae etiam sancti descendebant, quia nullus paradisum ingredi poterat, nullus portam regni coelestis intrare, donec Christus rhomphaeam igneam amoveret.
